Balance shaft
a counterweighted shaft driven from the crankshaft, at engine speed or twice engine speed, that cancels part of the primary or secondary shaking force.
Battery swapping
replacing a discharged traction battery with a charged one at a station in one to two minutes instead of charging it on the vehicle.
Brake thermal efficiency
the fraction of the fuel's chemical energy that an engine delivers as work at the crankshaft.
Cush drive
rubber blocks between the rear sprocket carrier and the wheel hub that absorb drive-line shocks.
False neutral
a gear lever position between two gears in which no gear is engaged, caused by an incomplete lever movement.
Final drive ratio
rear sprocket teeth divided by front sprocket teeth.
Free play
the movement of a lever, pedal or throttle before it starts to act, set so the control returns fully without dragging.
Gradient resistance
the component of weight acting down a slope, m × g × sin θ.
Hub motor
an electric motor built into the wheel hub; simple, but it adds unsprung mass.
Lean angle
the angle of the motorcycle from vertical in a turn; in a steady turn tan θ = v² / (g × r).
Mid-drive
an electric motor mounted in the frame that drives the rear wheel by chain or belt, keeping unsprung mass low.
Nut factor
the empirical constant K in T = K × d × F linking tightening torque to clamp load, about 0.20 dry and 0.15 oiled.
Outside micrometer
a screw-thread measuring instrument that reads external dimensions to 0.01 mm.
Overall ratio
the product of primary reduction, gear ratio and final drive ratio: engine turns per rear-wheel turn.
Power-to-mass ratio
maximum power divided by mass, in kW/kg; limited to 0.1 for L3e-A1 and 0.2 for L3e-A2.
Primary inertia force
the shaking force from the reciprocating piston and small end at crankshaft frequency.
Rolling radius
the effective radius of a loaded tyre, smaller than half its unloaded diameter.
Secondary inertia force
the shaking force at twice crankshaft frequency caused by connecting-rod angularity.
Screw extractor
a hardened, left-hand tapered tool driven into a drilled hole to unscrew a broken bolt.
Stoichiometric mixture
the air-fuel ratio at which all fuel and oxygen can react, 14.7:1 for petrol (λ = 1).
Thread insert
a coiled wire insert fitted in an oversize tapped hole to restore a damaged thread to its original size.
Three-way catalytic converter
an exhaust catalyst that converts HC, CO and NOx together, effective only near λ = 1.
Total indicator reading (TIR)
the difference between the highest and lowest dial gauge readings over one turn of a part.
Underbone
a frame with a single spine tube or pressed-steel backbone and the engine hung beneath it, used on step-throughs.
Waisted bolt
a bolt whose shank is thinner than its thread so that it stretches evenly under high load.
